provider: Telnyx Object Storage ($6/TB, zero metered egress)

free_tier.stated: Unlimited, $0.006 per GiB/month (≈$6.14/TB), no platform fee. Confirmed live: '$0.006per GB/mo', '$0platform fee', and the page's own worked example '10,000 GB STORED … $60.00'.

egress.terms: 'Egress fees | None'. This is the cheapest *combined* storage+egress number in this niche: $6/TB at rest with no egress metre at all, versus Bunny's $10 + $10 and CacheFly's $25 flat.

tooling: S3-compatible API; sign-up is self-serve ('SIGN UP FOR FREE' with a $0 PAYG tier). Operations are metred separately: $0.50/M state-change, $0.04/M state-read — negligible at blob-store access patterns but not at 1 TiB/day of small reads.
chaining: Take a free origin (Internet Archive at $0, or an anonymous host), front it with Telnyx storage only where you must, and the egress line disappears. At 20 TiB it is $123/mo with unlimited reads — cheaper than Hetzner BX41 (€40.60 ≈ $45 for 20 TB, and still the champion on pure price) but with S3 semantics and no per-connection shaping. Note their competitor table prices AWS S3 at '$0.023 + $0.09 egress' to make exactly this point.
limits_note: per-object-cap: none published. Request pricing is per-operation, so a workload of 10 KB objects at 1 TiB/day (~100M reads/day) would cost ~$4/day in state-reads — fine; a workload of 1 KiB objects would not be.
reliability_note: Already inventoried in A-P8 but only as a footnote; Card on file required for the PAYG tier. Their documented machine-readable endpoint GET /v2/public/pricing is 404 in practice — do not rely on it programmatically.

evidence.proved: '$0.006per GB/mo', '$0platform fee', 'Egress fees | None', example '10,000 GB STORED … $60.00'
